name: Question 14
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13954664/assets/8ea1ad85f30978bed681f48e02f4af2f401a1f561390bee09683ead252fc1d7d.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(1,-2)$ and passes through the point $(4,-3).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(1,-2),$ we substitute $h=1$ and $k=-2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(4,-3),$ so we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=-3$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-1) \\ (-3+2)^{2} & =4p(4-1) \\ 1 & =12p \\ p & =\frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-1) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{12})(x-1) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =\frac{1}{3}(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{1}{12}$ is positive.

Question 14
?

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?

a
(x−1)2=−13(y+2)
b
(y+2)2=13(x−1)
c
(y−2)2=112(x+1)
d
(y+2)2=−94(x−1)
e
(y+2)2=9(x−1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at (1,−2) and passes through the point (4,−3).

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is (h,k) and whose arms open right or left is given by (y−k)2=4p(x−h).

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at (h,k)=(1,−2), we substitute h=1 and k=−2 into the equation above and get (y+2)2=4p(x−1).

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point (4,−3), so we can substitute x=4 and y=−3 into the equation above and solve for p: (y+2)2=4p(x−1)(−3+2)2=4p(4−1)1=12pp=112 So, the equation of the parabola is (y+2)2=4p(x−1)(y+2)2=4(112)(x−1)(y+2)2=13(x−1).

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since p=112 is positive.
